models.description:
Model Card Summary: Plant Disease Detection Model
Model Overview
Transfer learning model (MobileNetV2) classifying plant leaf diseases into Healthy, Powdery Mildew, and Rust. Optimized for Android via Float16 quantization.

Key Specifications
Aspect	Detail
Input	224×224×3 RGB image
Output	3-class probability distribution
Model Size	4.57 MB (FP16 TFLite)
Accuracy	95%+ on test set
Inference	<50ms (Android), <20ms (Python)
Training Time	~15 minutes (Colab T4 GPU)
Architecture
Base: MobileNetV2 (ImageNet pre-trained, frozen)

Top: GlobalAvgPool → Dense(128, ReLU) → Dropout(0.2) → Dense(3, Softmax)

Total params: 2.4M (164K trainable)

Training Details
Dataset: 1,322 train / 60 val / 150 test images

Optimizer: Adam

Loss: Sparse Categorical Crossentropy

Epochs: 20 (early stopping at 15)

Augmentation: Random flip, rotation, zoom

Quantization
Type	Size	Accuracy Impact
Float16	4.57 MB	<0.5% loss
Dynamic	2.55 MB	~1% loss
Usage Limitations
Not for certified agricultural diagnosis

Requires centered, well-lit leaf images

Poor performance on blurry images or cluttered backgrounds

Not tested across multiple plant species

Ethics & Fairness
No demographic data involved

Balanced per-class performance (F1-scores: 0.94-0.96)

Not for regulatory or legal decisions

Should complement, not replace, expert consultation

Deployment
Android: TensorFlow Lite + classifier class

Python: TFLite Interpreter

Fully offline - no API calls required

models.description:
FedPrivNet is a custom hybrid deep learning model developed by Md. Sajjad Ullah
for multi-label chest X-ray disease classification across 14 thoracic pathologies.
The model is purpose-built for privacy-preserving federated learning environments.

ARCHITECTURE:

- Dual backbone: ResNet-18 + DenseNet-121 feature fusion
- GroupNorm throughout — fully DP-SGD compatible (no BatchNorm)
- Novel Spatial Attention Gate — built-in XAI heatmap module
- SE Channel Attention blocks in every residual stage
- 17,560,527 total parameters

BASELINE COMPARISON (same FL conditions, 3 epochs):

  ResNet-18 alone    → AUC: 0.7060  (11.2M params)
  DenseNet-121 alone → AUC: 0.6992  ( 7.0M params)
  FedPrivNet (Ours)  → AUC: 0.7862  (17.6M params)  ← BEST

  Improvement over ResNet-18    : +8.0% AUC
  Improvement over DenseNet-121 : +8.7% AUC

ABLATION STUDY (component contribution):

  Full FedPrivNet          → AUC: 0.6778  (reference)
  w/o Spatial Attention    → AUC: 0.6850  (drop: +0.0072)
  w/o SE Blocks            → AUC: 0.7018  (drop: +0.0239) ← largest
  w/o Attention & SE       → AUC: 0.6958  (drop: +0.0179)

  Key finding: SE Blocks contribute most to performance.
  Spatial Attention Gate provides diagnostic focus + XAI.

PERFORMANCE:

Mean AUC-ROC (14 classes)    : 0.7862
Train AUC-ROC                : 0.8913
Gender Demographic Parity Gap: 0.0059  (near zero — highly fair)
Age Demographic Parity Gap   : 0.0133  (near zero — highly fair)

Per-Class AUC-ROC:
  Cardiomegaly       0.8847  ████████████████████████████
  Emphysema          0.8698  ███████████████████████████
  Pneumothorax       0.8650  ███████████████████████████
  Edema              0.8358  ██████████████████████████
  Effusion           0.8297  ██████████████████████████
  Hernia             0.8138  █████████████████████████
  Mass               0.7785  ████████████████████████
  Fibrosis           0.7707  ████████████████████████
  Atelectasis        0.7617  ███████████████████████
  Pleural Thickening 0.7384  ██████████████████████
  Consolidation      0.7360  ██████████████████████
  Nodule             0.7148  █████████████████████
  Pneumonia          0.7122  █████████████████████
  Infiltration       0.6963  █████████████████████

TRAINING DETAILS:

Framework   : PyTorch 2.0
Optimizer   : AdamW (lr=1e-4, weight_decay=1e-5)
Scheduler   : CosineAnnealingLR
Loss        : Binary Cross Entropy
Batch Size  : 128
Epochs      : 30
Image Size  : 224 × 224
GPU         : NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090
Train Data  : 100,000 images (50k CXR8 + 50k CheXpert)
Val Data    : 10,000 images (CXR8 test set)

DATASETS USED:

- ChestX-ray14 — NIH Clinical Center
  112,120 frontal chest X-rays | 14 disease labels

- CheXpert-small — Stanford University
  224,316 chest X-rays | 14 observations

FILES IN THIS DATASET:

- FedPrivNet_best.pth                  — Model weights (201 MB)
- training_curves.png                  — Loss, AUC, fairness gap plots
- spatial_attention_visualization.png  — Built-in XAI heatmaps
- baseline_comparison.png             — ResNet-18 vs DenseNet-121 vs FedPrivNet
- ablation_study.png                  — Component contribution analysis
- training_history.json                — Full epoch-by-epoch training log

FEDERATED LEARNING PIPELINE:

  FedPrivNet backbone
        ↓
  Flower 1.7 — Federated Learning
        ↓
  Opacus 1.4 — DP-SGD (ε ∈ {1, 3, 5, 10})
        ↓
  Fairness Regularizer (Demographic Parity + Equal Opportunity)
        ↓
  Top-k Gradient Compression (k ∈ {0.30, 0.40, 0.50})
        ↓
  Grad-CAM + SHAP Explainability Analysis

LINKS:

HuggingFace : https://huggingface.co/mdsajjadullah/FedPrivNet-ChestXray14-CheXpert


AUTHOR:

Md. Sajjad Ullah
Department of Computer Science and Engineering
University of Asia Pacific, Bangladesh

models.description:
# Model Summary

This Kaggle model contains PyTorch checkpoints for the **Deepfake and Face Spoofing Detection System**, developed for the CO3201 Final Year Project at the University of Leicester.

The release contains multiple `.pth` checkpoints for video-based deepfake detection:

- **Mixed XceptionNet**: frame-level classifier trained on mixed datasets.
- **Ensemble model**: XceptionNet + EfficientNet-B4.
- **Temporal model**: frozen XceptionNet backbone with a 2-layer LSTM over frame sequences.
- **Robust model**: compression-aware fine-tuned XceptionNet variant.

The system detects whether a video is likely **REAL**, **FAKE**, or **INCONCLUSIVE** by sampling frames, detecting/aliging faces, classifying each face crop, and aggregating predictions into a video-level result.

Repository and dissertation release:  
https://github.com/raau1/Deepfake-and-Face-Spoofing-Detection-System/releases/tag/dissertation

## Usage

The checkpoints are PyTorch `.pth` files. The frame-level models accept normalized RGB face crops of shape:

```text
[B, 3, 299, 299]
```

and return logits of shape:

```text
[B, 2]
```

where the two classes are real/fake.

The temporal model accepts a sequence of aligned face crops:

```text
[B, T, 3, 299, 299]
```

with `T = 32`, and returns logits:

```text
[B, 2]
```

Example frame-level loading:

```python
import torch
from src.models.xception import create_xception

device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")

model = create_xception(num_classes=2, pretrained=False)
checkpoint = torch.load("outputs/models/mixed/best_model_mixed.pth", map_location=device)
state_dict = checkpoint.get("model_state_dict", checkpoint)

model.load_state_dict(state_dict)
model.to(device)
model.eval()

# Example input: batch of normalized RGB face crops
x = torch.randn(1, 3, 299, 299).to(device)

with torch.no_grad():
    logits = model(x)
    probs = torch.softmax(logits, dim=1)

fake_probability = probs[0, 1].item()
print(fake_probability)
```

For normal use, the repository’s FastAPI inference service is recommended because it performs the full preprocessing pipeline: video frame sampling, MTCNN face detection, MediaPipe face alignment, normalization, model inference, and aggregation.

Known preventable failures include videos with no detectable face, severe occlusion, extreme blur, heavy compression, side-profile faces, or manipulation methods very different from the training data.

## System

These checkpoints are part of a larger detection system, not a single standalone end-user model. The full system includes:

- OpenCV video decoding and uniform frame sampling.
- MTCNN face detection.
- MediaPipe FaceMesh-based face alignment.
- 299x299 RGB face crops.
- PyTorch model inference.
- Mean probability aggregation into a video-level verdict.
- Optional Grad-CAM explanations.
- Optional horizontal-flip test-time augmentation.
- A three-way verdict: REAL / FAKE / INCONCLUSIVE.

Downstream users should treat model outputs as decision-support signals, not as definitive proof of manipulation.

## Implementation Requirements

The reference implementation used:

- Python 3.11.9
- PyTorch 2.3.1 + CUDA 12.1
- torchvision 0.18.1
- timm
- OpenCV
- MediaPipe
- facenet-pytorch
- FastAPI
- NVIDIA RTX 4070 development GPU

Training is GPU-oriented and is impractical on CPU. Inference can run on CPU for small tests, but the intended deployment uses an NVIDIA GPU.

Measured end-to-end throughput was approximately **10.47 to 10.68 FPS** on an RTX 4070, including preprocessing and inference.

# Model Characteristics

## Model Initialization

The models were initialized from ImageNet-pretrained backbones where applicable:

- XceptionNet via `timm`
- EfficientNet-B4 via `timm`
- Temporal model using a frozen trained XceptionNet backbone plus a trained LSTM head

The checkpoints were then trained/fine-tuned for binary real/fake classification.

## Model Stats

Approximate model characteristics:

- XceptionNet: about **20.8M parameters**, checkpoint size about **238.6 MB**
- EfficientNet-B4 ensemble partner: about **17.5M parameters**
- Ensemble checkpoint: about **440.6 MB**
- Temporal model: frozen XceptionNet backbone + 2-layer LSTM, about **7.35M trainable parameters**, checkpoint size about **163.8 MB**
- Robust Xception checkpoint: about **238.6 MB**
- CBAM experimental checkpoint: about **244.6 MB**

The models are not quantized or pruned.

## Other Details

No differential privacy training was applied. No quantization, pruning, or model compression was applied to the released checkpoints.

# Data Overview

## Training Data

Training and evaluation used public deepfake datasets obtained from their original sources. Raw datasets are not redistributed with this model.

Datasets used across the project include:

- FaceForensics++
- Celeb-DF v2
- DeepFakeDetection
- DFDC
- WildDeepfake test subset

Preprocessing included:

- Uniform frame sampling from videos.
- Face detection using MTCNN.
- Face alignment using MediaPipe FaceMesh landmarks.
- 299x299 face crops with margin.
- Normalization before model inference.

Splits were performed at video level using an 80/10/10 train/validation/test split where applicable, to reduce identity leakage across splits.

## Demographic Groups

No explicit demographic labels were used for training or evaluation. Because subgroup labels such as age, gender, ethnicity, lighting condition, camera quality, and skin tone were not systematically annotated, the model card does not claim demographic fairness guarantees.

## Evaluation Data

Evaluation was performed on in-domain, cross-dataset, in-the-wild, and out-of-family datasets. The most important distinction is that DFDC contains manipulation methods not represented in the main training setup, making it a harder out-of-family benchmark.

# Evaluation Results

## Summary

Headline AUC/EER results from the dissertation and repository:

| Dataset | Best Model | AUC | EER |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| FaceForensics++ | Temporal | 99.87% | 1.20% |
| Celeb-DF v2 | Temporal | 99.99% | 0.23% |
| DeepFakeDetection | Temporal | 99.86% | 1.97% |
| WildDeepfake | Temporal | 91.54% | 13.86% |
| DFDC | Mixed v2 | 71.61% | 35.94% |

A key finding was that training only on FaceForensics++ generalized poorly to Celeb-DF v2, while mixed-dataset training significantly improved cross-dataset AUC.

## Subgroup Evaluation Results

No demographic subgroup evaluation was performed because demographic attributes were not available in a consistent annotated form. Evaluation was instead disaggregated by dataset/source, which showed strong performance on FaceForensics++, Celeb-DF v2, and DeepFakeDetection, lower performance on WildDeepfake, and substantially weaker performance on DFDC out-of-family data.

## Fairness

Fairness was treated primarily as robustness across datasets and manipulation sources rather than demographic parity. The project evaluated generalization across multiple deepfake datasets and manipulation families, but it did not establish formal fairness metrics across demographic groups.

## Usage Limitations

This model should not be used as the sole basis for high-stakes decisions. It is suitable for research, screening, triage, and decision support, but not for definitive attribution or automated enforcement.

Limitations include:

- Lower reliability on unseen manipulation methods.
- Sensitivity to face detection and alignment failures.
- Possible degradation on low-resolution, compressed, dark, occluded, or side-profile videos.
- No verified demographic fairness guarantees.
- A fake/real probability is not proof of authenticity or manipulation.

For responsible use, uncertain predictions should be reviewed manually, and the INCONCLUSIVE band should be preserved rather than forcing every result into a binary class.

## Ethics

The project considers deepfake detection as a defensive tool for media verification, moderation support, and research. Risks include false accusations, over-reliance on automated predictions, dataset bias, and misuse as a surveillance or identity-verification system.

Mitigations include:

- Reporting uncertainty through an INCONCLUSIVE prediction band.
- Providing Grad-CAM explanations for analyst inspection.
- Documenting cross-dataset generalization failures.
- Avoiding claims of perfect reliability.
- Releasing the model as a research artifact with known limitations.

These PyTorch model checkpoints were trained by me for the Deepfake and Spoofing Detection System project: https://github.com/raau1/Deepfake-and-Spoofing-Detection-System

The models are .pth checkpoints produced by the training scripts in that repository. They include XceptionNet, EfficientNet-B4 ensemble, temporal LSTM, and robustness fine-tuned variants for deepfake detection. Training and evaluation used datasets such as FaceForensics++, Celeb-DF, DFDC, and WildDeepfake-style evaluation data where applicable.
